2607.21558.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
2607.21558.paper_summary: Building socially calibrated large language models, which can learn from others without simply yielding to them, requires more than reducing sycophancy as a one-dimensional failure mode. Models must distinguish when to incorporate others' perspectives from when to maintain a well-grounded moral judgment. We study the broader resistance-compliance process governing this distinction. Across three studies, we show that models' judgment revision is structured along three dimensions that parallel classic phenomena in human social psychology: the distance between an incoming view and the model's initial position, the source attribution of that view, and the coalition structure supporting it. Models are generally more receptive to nearby positions, more influenced by views presented as their own prior judgments, and differently responsive to group pressure. These findings recast sycophancy as one expression of a broader judgment-updating process shaped by social influence. Our framework provides a principled basis for distinguishing constructive belief revision from sycophantic compliance, thereby supporting better alignment in morally consequential interactions.
2607.21558.paper_summary_zh: 建立社會調整的大型語言模型，這些模型能夠從他人那裡學習而不僅僅是屈從於他們，需要的不僅僅是將諂媚作為一種單一的失敗模式來減少。<lb/>模型必須區分何時應該納入他人的觀點以及何時應該保持良好的道德判斷。<lb/>我們研究了支配這一區別的更廣泛的抵抗-服從過程。<lb/>在三項研究中，我們顯示模型的判斷修訂是沿著三個維度結構化的，這些維度與人類社會心理學中的經典現象平行：進入觀點與模型初始立場之間的距離、該觀點的來源歸因，以及支持它的聯盟結構。<lb/>模型通常對附近的立場更具接受性，更受那些被呈現為其先前判斷的觀點影響，並且對群體壓力的反應有所不同。<lb/>這些發現將諂媚重新詮釋為一種更廣泛的判斷更新過程的表現，該過程受到社會影響的塑造。<lb/>我們的框架為區分建設性的信念修訂與諂媚的服從提供了一個原則性基礎，從而支持在道德上有重大影響的互動中更好的對齊。
